questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I considered several aspects of the destination including the culture in the country, the quality of my program at the university, my interest in the available subjects, and the size of the international and exchange community at the university/ in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Melbourne has a lot of online resources for exchange students, which made it easy to access any information I needed before and upon my arrival. They also had an orientation scheduled for all new exchange students with all the information we needed. It's also possible to show up in person at Stop 1 for personal assistance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to visit stop 1 for help regestering in one of my subjects. I had problems with assigning myself to the subject as it requires a prerequisite and my documentation for the prerequisite had to be approved by the course coordinator. I had uploaded it in my initial application to the university, and then the university was supposed to get the approval for me. However, they had not gotten it before I arrived, but made sure I got it after I contacted them at Stop 1. It took some time, but it got sorted out eventually.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would advice anyone going to University of Melbourne to not hesitate contacting stop 1 for help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The university has a few accomodation options for exchage students and I chose this out of easy, as it can be difficult to find housing in Melbourne, and the accomodation was ideally located next to my campus, close to the city center, and in a nice neighbourhood.

I chose the accomodation that's only for master and phd students, which I've been very happy with, as people were generally a bit older and most had tried to live on their own before. That definitely contributed to the kind of dynamic I was hoping for. 

The accomodation was definitely expensive, but overall it was worth it for me as I got a large network of international and exchange students at my accomodation, many who became my good friends and people I travelled with during my stay. It was also in walking distance to many things, which I enjoyed as I didn't have a bike.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared appartment with three other girls, and we all shared the kitchen. Furthermore, there were a shared kitchen on the 1st and the 14th floor of the accomodation, which we sometimes used for cooking together among friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's expensive, but also an easy way to find housing, and many other avaiilable housing types are not necessarily that much cheaper. It's also a great way to connect with other students if you're interested in that. It's mainly international and exchange students who live there, but also a few Australians. My accomodation offered monthly events with activities, food, etc. and by attending those in the beginning of my stay, I met a lot of people.

questions.answer: I was easy as the university made a guideline on how to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could make an online request for help or show up at stop 1.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. They often offer more than class within each subject, but I managed to get both classes on campus and at the times I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to ask for help at Stop 1.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience the classes are overall easier than I'm used to at home. It differs from subject to subject, but it is definitely easier to achieve a good grade with less effort. That said I definitely felt like I learned something in my classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Every professor have their own style of teaching just like at home, and some styles of teaching suits me better than others, just like at home. The biggest differences was the structure of the grading, as we are used to one final exam at the end of the year, whereas at UniMelb I had at least two assignments in each subject that counted towards my final grade. In some of my classes I also had group presentations that were graded. The experience of working in groups was very different from what I'm used to. It felt more like individual work that we collected into a group presentation, rather than a group effort. Furthermore, we were assigned groups and didn't have any say about who we wanted to work with. Even though it's more time consuming, I definitely prefer doing group work the way I'm used to from home, as I learn more that way and the result is better.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bioethics in Practice 
Infectious Disease Epidemiology
Gender & Health 
Nutrition Politics and Policy

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed both Bioethics in Practice and Infectious Disease Epidemiology. 

We only get a brief introduction to ethics in our program at home, and I think it's really interesting to learn how to apply ethics in practice. I really liked the professor and there was a nice dynamic in the classroom, with many great discussions throughout the semester. 

I enjoyed Infectious Disease Epidemiology as it was nice to dive into a specific branch of epidemiology. The professor was also really good, the class material was really interesting and this was definitely the subject where I learned the most.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot more on groceries than I'm used to at home, and I spend more money eating out than I usually do. Some items are more expensive than in Denmark, while some are less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a lot of opportunities and they have a day where all the clubs and sports clubs are presented, however, I never joined one as there was so much going on all the time and I didn't find the time for it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seams like there is something for everyone. They have a list on their website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There are many free or low-cost activities and events around the city all year around, but especially in the summer, such as free concerts, free festivals, and night markets. Make sure to do some research and use the city as much as you can. 
I would also recomend to travel either on longer trips, weekend trips, or day trips. There are many beautiful places in Australia. For most of them I would recomend renting a car, so make sure to get an international drivers licence before leaving for Australia.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the national parks all around Australia, for a weekend trip 'the Grampians' or Phillip Island is very nice. Take the train to the beaches, go to museum (many are free), see the city from the Skydeck, go to Queen Victoria Market (or night market), explore Fitzroy, Carlton, or Brunswich. Go to Fitzroy market in weekends, and go for coffee often - it's good and cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is the most 'European' city in Australia and is full of international students. It always takes some time to adjust to a new place, but overall it was easy for me to adjust and I felt comfortable and at home in Melbourne.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: NA.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the people in Australia and the laid back feeling.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember to enjoy the city and travel as much as you can
- Ask if you have any questions, there are plenty of resources at uni to help you 
- Get some friends who are also on exchange, as they are at the same situation as you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of the above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met was the best part, as they contributed to makinng the experience even better.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting settled in a new routine in my new soroundings

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
